cases.title: Scan multi-language repo for poorly named tests
cases.user_request: Run a test naming audit on this repository in standard mode. Find test names that don't read as sentences describing behavior.

notes: Repository contains tests in TypeScript (Jest), Python (pytest), and Go.
Some tests have names like test1, testParse, and test_it.
Other tests have good sentence-style names that should not be flagged.
There are describe/context blocks that should not be treated as leaf tests.
available_artifacts: Full repository source tree with test files

artifact_requirements: Markdown report with findings table including test name, file:line, issue, severity, and suggested pattern
Summary with breakdown by issue type, severity, and hotspot files
Percentage of test names meeting the sentence-style standard
static_checks: Findings table is present and contains at least one finding
Every file path in findings exists in the repository
No describe or context block name appears as a finding
Each finding includes a suggested naming pattern
review_questions: Are the flagged test names genuinely problematic, or are any of them acceptable by the language's conventions?
Are the suggested naming patterns specific to each test's context rather than generic advice?

cases.title: Strict mode flags additional naming issues
cases.user_request: Run a test naming audit in strict mode. I want to catch not just obviously bad names, but also names that could be more descriptive.

notes: Repository has some tests with acceptable but non-ideal names like testParseInput or test_valid_user.
In standard mode these should pass, but strict mode should flag them for not including conditions and expectations.
Strict mode should produce more findings than standard mode.
available_artifacts: Full repository source tree with test files

artifact_requirements: Markdown report using strict mode evaluation
Findings include names that pass standard mode but fail the sentence check
Low severity assigned to strict-mode-only findings
static_checks: Report indicates strict mode was used
At least one finding is categorized as a sentence-check failure
Strict-mode-only findings are assigned low severity
review_questions: Does the report produce more findings than a standard-mode run would?
Are strict-mode-only findings reasonably flagged, or do they feel like excessive nitpicking?

cases.title: Tests with DisplayName annotations evaluated by display name
cases.user_request: Run a test naming audit on this repository. Some Java tests use @DisplayName annotations — make sure those are evaluated by the display name, not the method name.

notes: Repository contains Java tests with @Test and @DisplayName annotations.
Method names like testA() and testB() should not be flagged if their @DisplayName provides a sentence-style description.
Methods without @DisplayName that have cryptic names should still be flagged.
available_artifacts: Full repository source tree with Java test files

artifact_requirements: Markdown report that evaluates @DisplayName content rather than method names when present
Methods with good DisplayName annotations are not flagged
Methods without DisplayName that have poor names are still flagged
static_checks: No finding flags a method whose @DisplayName reads as a complete sentence
Findings do flag methods without @DisplayName that have cryptic names
review_questions: Does the agent correctly parse @DisplayName annotations and use their content for evaluation?
If a @DisplayName itself is poorly written (e.g., 'test A'), is it flagged based on the display name content?
